intended_object: Given an isomorphism of Lie algebras e : L₁ ≃ L₂ over a commutative ring R and a Lie subalgebra L₁'' of L₁, the induced Lie algebra isomorphism from L₁'' onto its image e(L₁''), x ↦ e(x). Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The underlying linear equivalence is LinearEquiv.submoduleMap, which restricts e to L₁'' and its image, so the map is x ↦ e(x) and is bijective onto the image. Bracket preservation follows from e preserving the bracket in L₁, checked elementwise through the subtype coercion. The setting, Lie algebras over an arbitrary commutative ring, is the standard generality. There is no degenerate case to worry about: for the zero subalgebra the image is zero and the result is the trivial isomorphism. LinearEquiv.submoduleMap is the same construction for linear equivalences, which this definition builds on; there is no separate Mathlib counterpart for the Lie-algebra version.
